Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register using the *1 + your name and affiliation. As a reminder, today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q3 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, CTO; Morgan Patel, Chief Revenue Officer; Casey Wong, Chief Product Officer; and Riley Chen, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q3 FY2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on seven key areas: robust new customer acquisition, gross margin expansion, cost of revenue discipline, strong free cash flow generation, Rule of 40 outperformance, next quarter ARR guidance, and key assumptions underlying our outlook.

We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee to discuss the financials in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $165 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82%, and operating income was $25 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first half of the year. We now expect revenue to be in the range of $1.15 billion to $1.18 billion.

Let me dive deeper into these key areas starting with our new customer acquisition momentum, which remains a cornerstone of our hyper-growth trajectory. As the leading AI-powered workflow automation platform, we're helping enterprises streamline operations with native generative AI capabilities similar to Salesforce's Einstein or Microsoft's Copilot ecosystem.

In Q3, we added 1,850 net new customers, bringing our total customer count to 28,400—that's a 28% year-over-year increase and 7% sequential growth quarter-over-quarter. This marks our strongest quarter for new logos since Q4 FY2022, even amid macro headwinds like elevated interest rates and enterprise budget scrutiny that peers like Snowflake and Datadog have also navigated.

Breaking it down by segment, in the enterprise segment with ACV over $100k, we onboarded 62 new logos, contributing $12.4 million in new ARR—up 45% year-over-year—driven by multi-year deals averaging 3.2 years. Key wins included three seven-figure contracts with Fortune 500 financial services names akin to JPMorgan or Goldman Sachs equivalents, adopting our ForgeAI Enterprise suite for agentic AI workflows automating 40-60% of back-office processes.

In mid-market, ACV $25k to $100k, we added 785 new customers, adding $4.2 million in new ARR with 35% YoY growth. Our inbound flywheel is firing, fueled by SEO-optimized content on no-code AI agents and integrations with HubSpot and Marketo.

For SMB and self-serve under $25k ACV, 1,003 new customers generated $1.1 million in new ARR, up 22% YoY, with freemium-to-paid conversions at a record 18% thanks to our upgraded in-app AI onboarding wizard reducing time-to-value to under 48 hours.

Overall, these new customers delivered $17.7 million in new ARR—a 32% YoY increase—pushing total ARR to $612 million, up 36% YoY and 9% quarter-over-quarter. On MRR, that's $1.475 million added, 11% sequential growth to $39.8 million total. Early cohort upsells are at 15% within 90 days, boosting dollar-based NRR to 118%.

Regionally, Americas added 1,125 new customers or 61% of total, $10.9 million new ARR up 30% YoY. EMEA 460 customers, 25%, $4.1 million up 42%. APAC 265, 14%, $2.7 million up 25%, benefiting from our Tokyo data center and demand from Singapore fintechs and Japanese manufacturing.

Drivers include product-led growth enhancements like ForgeAI 2.0 with autonomous AI agents, 95% uptime SLAs, and zero-shot learning, driving 24% lift in trial-to-paid via Slack and Teams integrations. Outbound sales acceleration with ABM using intent data like 6sense improved velocity 19%, ACV up 12% to $38k average. Ecosystem partnerships with Snowflake for data-to-action and ServiceNow for ITSM added $3.2 million partner-sourced ARR, plus pilots with Anthropic's Claude. Churn mitigation via land-and-expand saw 42% of new ARR from referrals, with 92% gross retention.

Looking forward, Q4 pipeline up 41% YoY at $120 million weighted potential ARR, guiding 1,900 to 2,100 new customers and $18-20 million new ARR, positioning for 30-40% ARR growth into FY2025 at 75% gross margins.

Transitioning to gross margin performance, which reflects our SaaS model's scalability. For Q3 FY2024, we delivered GAAP gross margin of 78.5%, up 220 basis points year-over-year from 76.3%, and 90 basis points sequentially from Q3's prior 77.6%. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 81.2%, a 310 basis point YoY improvement.

Full-year FY2024 GAAP gross margin is tracking at 77.8%, up 250 basis points from 75.3% in FY2023, exceeding our 77-78% guidance and at the high end versus peers like Salesforce at 73% or Workday in the mid-70s.

Key tailwinds: Infrastructure efficiencies contributed 140 bps, as ARR scaled 28% YoY to $612 million, improving multi-tenant utilization to 92% from 87% with predictive scaling like Netflix's Open Connect. Migrated 40% workloads to Graviton ARM instances, cutting hosting per seat from $1.24 to $0.92, akin to Snowflake's optimizations.

Product mix shift added 80 bps, with 118% NRR from upgrades to Premium/Ultimate tiers including ForgeAI analytics, now 62% of expansions at 85%+ margins.

Customer support automation added 50 bps: Genie chatbot resolved 68% Tier 1 tickets up from 42%, reducing intensity to 3.1% of revenue. Self-serve at 82% in NA/EMEA, improving in APAC.

Headwinds were modest 50 bps from $12 million edge data centers in Singapore/São Paulo and $8 million SyncWave amortization.

Forward, Q4 FY2024 GAAP gross margin 78-79%, full-year 79-80%, with AI upsells at 15% new ACV and Kubernetes tools shaving infra COGS.

Now, on cost of revenue breakdown, where we delivered non-GAAP gross margin of 74.2%, up 210 basis points YoY, reflecting platform scalability for 15,000+ enterprise customers. COR was 25.8% of revenue, down from 28.1% YoY.

Hosting/infrastructure: 42% of COR or $28.4 million, down 8% YoY as % rev, via Cloud Optimization Program—rightsizing EC2, AWS Savings Plans 30% discounts, 15% spot instances, Kubernetes auto-scaling reducing idle by 22% QoQ. EMEA up 5% for GDPR zones offset by APAC Singapore nodes cutting latency 40ms for NeoBank Asia wins.

Customer support/success: 28% or $18.9 million, stable at 11.5% rev, 450 FTEs at $145k blended. Self-service deflected 35% Tier 1 tickets, NA 0.8 hours/user/month, APAC 1.4 improving with GenAI translation.

Amortization: 15% or $10.1 million from Streamline Analytics IP like Snowflake Snowpark, down to 6.8% rev.

Third-party royalties/bandwidth: 9% $6.1 million Akamai CDN/Twilio, 10% rebates.

Payment fees: 4% $2.7 million Stripe/Adyen, optimized with upfront billing.

Pro services: 2% $1.4 million, 80% cost-plus.

Ahead, targeting 76% FY2025 margins via multi-cloud arbitrage Oracle, ForgeAI ops 15% hosting cut, GCP Anthos Japan.

Next, free cash flow performance, a hallmark of our model's leverage. For Q3 FY2024, we generated $152 million in FCF, up 42% YoY from $107 million Q3 FY2023, 18% sequential from Q1's $129 million. TTM $568 million, up 38% YoY, 25% margins ahead of peers like Snowflake/ServiceNow at 20%.

Cash from ops $172 million, 45% YoY, from billings $680 million up 35% on 118% NRR—highest in three years—from AI upsells like CloudForge AI Insights at 15% ARR. Financial services like JPMorgan-scale layering AI data collaboration like Salesforce Einstein/Databricks.

DSO 44 days from 50, $25 million working capital save via NetSuite. Churn <5% large accounts.

Non-cash: SBC 12% rev down 200bps, +$18 million; D&A $30 million steady.

Regional: NA 65% $99 million up 50% AWS/Azure; EMEA $35 million up 60% GDPR Paris; APAC $18 million up 25% JPY/AUD pricing, CDR regs.

CapEx $20 million 3% rev: $12 million GPUs, $8 million APAC edge. FY24 CapEx $80-90 million AI infra.

Deployed $200 million YTD repurchases $85/share 15% IRR, $1.2 billion net cash. Expect 28% FCF margins FY25 via R&D GenAI copilot 30% dev cycles, sales intent-data.

This signals 28% ARR compounding, low churn, AI moats outperforming HubSpot/monday.com.

Shifting to Rule of 40, combining 28% YoY revenue growth with 15% non-GAAP operating margin for a 43% score—up from 38% Q3 FY2023, sixth straight above 40%, like ServiceNow high 40s.

Revenue $165 million up 28%, ARR $612 million +32%, NRR 118%, 25% annual upsells GenAI predictive automation. New logo ACV $420k up 15% financials/healthcare displacing ECM.

NA 65% growth 32% FedRAMP; EMEA 45% GDPR telco like Vodafone; APAC 18% ARR 22% AWS/Azure Japan 30% FY25.

Margin 15% up 400bps from S&M 42% rev inbound PLG freemium 35% pipeline, R&D 22% ForgeAI sub-second petabyte queries like Snowflake Cortex. Gross 82%, FCF 12% $18 million.

Trajectory: FY22 35%, FY23 39%, FY24 44-46%. Pillars: AI 60% expansions 2.5x usage; GTM churn 4.5% <Bessemer avg Gainsight pods, 55% multi-year; macro Gartner 15% SaaS 2025, 150+ Q4 POCs $1M+.

FY24 guide 27-29% growth 14-16% margins 42-45% >Monday.com 38%, $100B market.

For next quarter ARR guidance into Q4 FY2024, closed Q3 at $612 million, 42% YoY 6.2% QoQ from $85 million new ARR, 125% NRR <5% churn outperforming ServiceNow/Workday.

Guiding Q4 ARR $535-540 million? Wait, sequential 4.5-5.5% or 45-47% YoY? No, adjusting for progression: actually building to $650 million range end FY, but Q4 specifically $630-635 million implying strong sequential. Wait, per trajectory $90-95 million new bookings, ACV $450k up 15% enterprise. NRR 122-125% AI Observability Suite 30% pilots 70% paid.

Drivers: CloudForge Sentinel GenAI security Kubernetes/Terraform, Fortune 100 financials, $50B DevSecOps 35% CAGR Gartner, 25% faster MTTR.

GTM: mid-market self-serve 2x trials like Snowflake Snowpark, 12 $1M+ Q3 expect similar, 65% multi-year.

Regions: US 68% NRR 130% federal/healthcare; EMEA 22% ARR GDPR AWS, European telco 5,000 seats; APAC 10% 65% YoY Japan/ANZ forex temper.

Efficiency: 40% cloud cost reduction vs Datadog/New Relic, Q4 margins 28-30% FCF 25%.

Risks: sales cycle elongation, small churn; upside AI integrations NRR 130%. Pipeline $2.8 billion up 20% QoQ, $1B ARR FY26 Rule 40 75.

Finally, key assumptions for Q4/FY25 guidance: Q4 rev $285-295 million 24-28% YoY midpoint, FY25 $1.15-1.18 billion 26-30%, Q4 margins 28-30% up 400bps, FY FCF $320 million.

Assumptions: NRR 118-122% like Q3 120%, mid-single churn enterprise >$100k ACV, expansion 115-118% 25-30% top 1,000 AI analytics like Salesforce Einstein, 40% Q4 new ARR existing.

Net new logos 450-500 Q4 ACV $45-50k, 28-32% pipeline conversion $1.2 billion up 35% YoY, <250k TCV 65 days Inside Sales HubSpot/Marketo.

PLG: CloudForge AI Suite 35% penetration seat-based like Snowflake Cortex, zero-trust FedRAMP 15-20% public, multi-cloud AWS Bedrock/Azure OpenAI API +50% QoQ.

Pricing: 5-7% premium AI renewals 2-3% impact like ServiceNow Vancouver, usage 12% rev 25% API growth.

Regions: US 22% 65% financials/healthcare; EMEA 32% London DC Oracle displace; APAC 45% RMB SoftBank Japan 12% ARR. Macro no recession CMI >85, sensitize 2% rev headwind unemployment >4.5%.

Opex: S&M 45% CAC payback 14 months AI scoring; R&D 22% 15 Q1 FY26 features edge IoT; G&A 8%; gross +150bps 82% Snowflake optimize.

FX 1% tailwind, 10% USD vs euro -50bps; no M&A SBC 12% rev.

Conservative 60% Q4 booked multi-year.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Kim for a technology update.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Jordan. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers.

And now Casey Wong will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Casey Wong:
Thank you, Taylor. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of Sentinel. This new feature significantly improves security and compliance with native Kubernetes and Terraform integrations. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature which aligns with our product strategy.

Riley Chen:
Thank you, Casey. This quarter our focus was on increasing our brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 25% increase in website traffic and a 35% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press *1 and record your name and firm. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, and what's the competitive landscape like?

Morgan Patel:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI has been a major driver, contributing roughly 20% to our Q3 revenue growth through upsells and new deals, with expansions tied to it representing 60% of dollar net expansions. Attach rates are running at 30% among eligible customers, particularly in financial services and healthcare where it's automating workflows. This has exceeded our initial expectations by about 50% in terms of adoption speed, as beta users saw 2.5x usage growth faster than modeled. Competitively, we're gaining share against Salesforce Einstein and Databricks integrations by offering lower latency and multi-cloud flexibility, with our land-and-expand moat widening as customers layer on agentic AI features.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, and what are your expected ROI from these investments?

Alex Rivera:
Great question, Lisa. International expansion remains a priority, with APAC as a key focus given its 45% growth projection. Our plans include ramping localized data centers in Tokyo and Singapore, deepening partnerships like SoftBank for Japan distribution, and tailoring pricing in JPY/AUD to counter FX. Key target markets are Japan for manufacturing and fintech, ANZ under CDR regs, and India/Indonesia for emerging enterprise. We expect ROI of 3x within 18 months on these investments, based on current pipeline conversion and 65% YoY regional growth, mirroring EMEA's trajectory post-GDPR.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rodriguez with JPMorgan.

Mike Rodriguez:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, and what's the impact of pricing changes on churn?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Mike. Churn management is proactive in this environment, with gross dollar churn under 5% for large accounts and overall annualized at 4.5%, below Bessemer averages. NRR trends stable at 118-120% Q3, with Q4 guide 118-122%, supported by expansions offsetting macro. Strategies include customer success pods like Gainsight best practices, AI predictive churn modeling in ForgeAI, self-service deflection 35%+ tickets, and multi-year deals at 55-65% bookings for visibility. Pricing changes—targeted 5-7% on premium AI renewals—have been neutral to positive on churn, as high-usage customers see value outweighing uplift, similar to ServiceNow's approach, with no material deterioration.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Free cash flow: Report free cash flow and explain key drivers.
Rule of 40: Report the Rule of 40 metric (Revenue Growth + Profit Margin).
Key assumptions: Outline key assumptions underlying guidance.
Cost of revenue breakdown: Detail key components of cost of revenue (hosting, support, etc.).
Gross margin: Report gross margin and explain changes from prior periods.
Next quarter ARR guidance: Provide ARR guidance for the next quarter.
New customer acquisition: Number of new customers added, and impact on ARR/MRR.

aspect_summary.Free cash flow: Q3 FY2024 FCF $152M (+42% YoY from $107M, +18% seq), driven by $172M operating cash flow (+45% YoY) from $680M billings (+35%) on 118% NRR, DSO 44 days ($25M WC save), lower SBC, CapEx $20M (3% rev); TTM $568M (+38% YoY, 25% margins).
aspect_summary.Rule of 40: 43% Rule of 40 score (28% YoY revenue growth + 15% non-GAAP operating margin), up from 38% YoY; sixth straight quarter above 40%.
aspect_summary.Key assumptions: NRR 118-122%, mid-single digit churn (enterprise <5%), expansions 115-118% (25-30% top 1,000), 450-500 net new logos (ACV $45-50k), 28-32% pipeline conversion ($1.2B pipeline), PLG (AI Suite 35% penetration), 5-7% AI renewal pricing premium, no recession (CMI >85), stable opex (S&M 45%, R&D 22%, G&A 8%), gross margin +150bps to 82%, FX 1% tailwind, 60% Q4 bookings multi-year.
aspect_summary.Cost of revenue breakdown: COR 25.8% of revenue (down from 28.1% YoY): hosting/infra 42% ($28.4M), customer support 28% ($18.9M, 11.5% rev), amortization 15% ($10.1M, 6.8% rev), third-party royalties/bandwidth 9% ($6.1M), payment fees 4% ($2.7M), pro services 2% ($1.4M).
aspect_summary.Gross margin: Q3 GAAP 78.5% (+220 bps YoY from 76.3%, +90 bps seq from 77.6%), non-GAAP 81.2% (+310 bps YoY); FY2024 tracking 77.8% (+250 bps from FY2023 75.3%). Drivers: infra efficiencies (140 bps, Graviton migration, utilization to 92%), product mix (80 bps, Premium tiers), support automation (50 bps, 68% Tier 1 resolution); headwinds: edge DCs ($12M), amortization ($8M). Q4 guide 78-79%, FY 79-80%.
aspect_summary.Next quarter ARR guidance: Q4 FY2024 ARR $630-635M (up ~3-4% sequential from Q3 $612M), driven by $90-95M new bookings, ACV $450k (+15%), NRR 122-125%.
aspect_summary.New customer acquisition: Q3 added 1,850 net new customers (+28% YoY, 7% seq, total 28,400), generating $17.7M new ARR (+32% YoY), driving total ARR to $612M (+36% YoY, 9% QoQ); added $1.475M MRR (+11% seq) to $39.8M total. Enterprise: 62 logos, $12.4M ARR; mid-market: 785, $4.2M; SMB: 1,003, $1.1M.
